notes: Canonical combat job: protection through physical intervention and field medicine.

Betty must read as cute and sexy before she reads as realistic. The approved visual language is premium adult anime-fantasy: bright eyes, freckles, auburn curls, confident flirtatious energy, a fitted tobacco leather bodice over warm ivory lace, dark leather short field shorts, tall brown boots and one restrained green-and-navy tartan hip sash.
Locked body direction: slight agile adult frame, modest small chest, narrow hips, fine waist and long lean legs. Do not drift toward voluptuous, heavy-hourglass or physically bulky anatomy.

art.accessibilityDescription: An adult human inventor-captain with a lean 1850s American frontier silhouette: weathered slouch hat, dark sea coat, boots, brass echo compass, compact boiler pack, steam repeating carbine, experimental sidearm and cutlass.

metadata.narrativeAuthoringRule: Every protagonist and heroine must have a personal history, a present pressure, a household life, a specific relationship progression, and a contribution outside combat before the character is production-ready.
notes: Full canonical name: Captain Michael Corrigan. Title cards and ordinary dialogue use Michael; Captain Corrigan is the formal or professional address.

Michael is visible in every battle roster and his command deck is exposed: Weapon Attack and Reposition are authored combat records he can be given as orders. Echo and Field Order are authored later, as their own records.

Before the island he commanded the Handsome Jack, an old tea cutter already obsolete by the time of Commodore Perry's expedition. A later owner fitted it with a steam engine too powerful and poorly balanced for the hull.

The engine's weight and thrust made the Handsome Jack fast in fair water. In the typhoon that wrecked the expedition, the overloaded machinery and unstable hull tore the ship apart. Michael survived the wreck; the Handsome Jack did not.

His player-facing silhouette is American frontier circa the 1850s: lean, weathered, practical, with a slouch hat and gun belt. He reads as a cowboy who has also survived a sea wreck, not as a uniformed naval officer.

His loadout is steampunk. The Handsome Jack steam carbine, experimental sidearm, cutlass, compact boiler pack, brass tools and echo compass must look like one repairable field kit rather than unrelated costume props.

He is a genius inventor. Each heroine teaches him a real method from her own discipline; he adapts those methods into expedition hardware with her knowledge and approval. Their relationships drive shared discovery and household projects, never extraction of an ability from a passive companion.
Echo abilities are mechanically distinct from heroine bond skills and must be authored as their own combat records before they become player commands.
The paper card is a contract for rail scale, silhouette and costume read; it is not a substitute for final character art.

animationBeats.pose: The tide spawn unfolds an eye that should not exist and turns its full attention on the target, motionless.

value.doctrine: Provisional (brief section 6.2): a centralized administrative and military occupation faction built on ports, roads, forts, standardized production, taxation, artillery and external supply. Proposed strengths: disciplined forces, fortification, artillery, standardization, ports, major-road logistics, administrative control, external reinforcement. Proposed weaknesses: rigid command, expensive occupation, long supply chains, isolated garrisons, dependence on ports and formal routes, and resistance by local populations. Prose only; nothing in the strategy tree may branch on it before S15.

value.displayName: The Ward She Did Not Have to Hold

beats.text: PLACEHOLDER PROSE. Ayla sets a ward line across a doorway that is not hers to defend, for people who are not hers, and holds it longer than the reading justifies.
PLACEHOLDER PROSE. Afterward she argues with Michael about the tomb rather than about herself. She is a scholar first, and the fastest route to her attention is a problem she has not solved.
PLACEHOLDER PROSE. He can take her reading, argue it, or hand her the machine and let her test it. She is measuring whether he wants her work or her agreement.

notes: Placeholder prose. Every beat text is a stand-in; final lines are unwritten and are not approved dialogue.

Ayla has no content/characters/ayla.json yet -- that record is C3's lane, blocked on A7/H5. She is nonetheless one of the two established women, so her scenes are authored against her stable ID and the validator names her as the one womanId whose character record is still pending.
The scene is about the tomb, not about Michael. Brief section 5.6: recruitment must not dominate every scene; attraction is the secondary layer here.
presentationLevel is fade_to_black; the adult pack overrides beats by ID and is a separate artifact (C8/B10/E9).

beats.text: PLACEHOLDER PROSE. Ayla tells Michael what the tomb is actually for, which is not what her own people have been told, and watches his face while she says it.

PLACEHOLDER PROSE. She offers to keep telling him -- from where she stands, without leaving it. She is not joining. She is choosing to be his way in, which is a different and possibly permanent thing.
PLACEHOLDER PROSE. She stays until the lamp is low, and neither of them pretends the evening was only about the tomb. The scene closes there.

notes: Placeholder prose. Every beat text is a stand-in; final lines are unwritten and are not approved dialogue.
Contact is a real and possibly permanent stage, not a way-point: brief section 5.6's attraction-without-immediate-defection list. This scene deliberately does not advance her toward Committed.
TrustInMichael carries the rule, and it is above the floor S12's test cares about; PerceivedOpportunity is the second half of her actual motive.
The fade beat is last and is the whole of what the base game shows; the adult pack overrides it by ID (C8/B10/E9).
Ayla's character record is C3's lane and does not exist yet.

beats.text: PLACEHOLDER PROSE. She comes to him. Courtship in this game is not one-directional (brief section 5.6), and Betty has never in her life waited to be chosen.

PLACEHOLDER PROSE. She says what she wants plainly, and then says the harder thing: that she is asking to stay, that this is her joining, and that she wants it said out loud before anything else happens.
PLACEHOLDER PROSE. Michael answers her in kind or does not. Either answer is a real one; the arc does not punish him for the second and does not pretend the first cost nothing.
PLACEHOLDER PROSE. She leaves the lamp burning, which in her whole life she has never done for anyone, and the scene closes there.

beats.text: PLACEHOLDER PROSE. Betty takes the second watch without being asked and without announcing it, because the man who had it is the man whose ribs she set that afternoon.
PLACEHOLDER PROSE. She asks Michael what he intends to build here, and does not accept the short answer. She has buried enough people to have earned the long one.
PLACEHOLDER PROSE. Michael tells her the truth, tells her half of it, or asks her a question back. She is looking for whether he treats her as crew or as an audience.

notes: Placeholder prose. Every beat text is a stand-in written to prove the record shape and the beat kinds; final lines are unwritten and are not approved dialogue.
The opening beat of Betty's arc: awareness becomes interest. Interest is an opening and nothing more (brief section 5.6).

PLACEHOLDER PROSE. Afterward she tells him what she will do for him and what she will not, in that order, and means both. This is the first thing she has promised anyone since the ship went down.

requiredFeatures: one climb toward the damaged estate

readableDescriptions.text: The Handsome Jack lies split along the black sand below the tide line. Her overlarge steam engine has torn the old tea cutter open, leaving copper pipe, wet timber and a climb toward shelter.
The boiler housing is still warm enough to steam in the rain. Its cracked braces show why the cutter rolled badly in the typhoon, and a careful inspection can recover a useful part.

requiredFeatures: river path through the garden wall

readableDescriptions.text: The estate was built as a coastal refuge, not a fortress. One veranda rail hangs loose after the storm, while the infirmary table, armory alcove and kitchen still make it a usable home base.
Beyond the garden wall, a narrow stone track drops toward a river landing. The gate can be barred against wandering monsters, but it is not a permanent barrier to the island at night.

estateConsequenceResponses.text: Betty has marked the river gate with a simple brass alarm line. A heavy animal crossing the path will wake the household before it reaches the veranda.

readableDescriptions.text: The ramp was cut for a procession of honored dead. Bronze name plaques line the wet stone, and several bear scratches where someone has tried to remove names that keep returning.

At the top of the ramp, the inner door stands under a fractured bronze arch, open on the threshold of the tomb. It is a destination beyond the first route, not an empty backdrop or a doorway the party can fake open.

battleEntries.aftermathDescription: The razorbeak has fled into the jungle. The broken lane is clear, and the processional ramp is open.

readableDescriptions.text: The terrace was built to receive a procession. Vines now use its bronze-green seams as ladders, and the carved gate beyond it has watched enough storms to look patient.
The broken paving opens into a clear lane between two fallen slabs. Something large has crossed it recently, leaving clawed cuts through the wet moss.
A bronze-green marker points inland beside the broken jetty. Its old road symbol is still clear: the stone route is slower and exposed, while the jungle edge closes distance under heavy cover.
The river is too deep and slow for a casual crossing. A cargo skiff has been smashed against the landing, making the estate path and the old reception road the two useful ways forward.

requiredFeatures: racked register plates in working order
dry air and no water damage
one way back to the reception
elven civic record-keeping, not burial goods

readableDescriptions.text: The ledger is intact and still being written. Names struck from the registers outside are entered again here in a later hand, which is the plain reason the island calls this the Tomb of Returning Names.

requiredFeatures: round elven truth space with three named ways out
sealed archive door with no visible mechanism
low service opening at floor level

readableDescriptions.text: The speaking stone gives back one name in full, the way the dead were recorded rather than the way they were called. Reading it aloud is what the archive door was cut to hear, and the low service opening is the only other way on.

requiredFeatures: grave goods pulled out and left disturbed
two ways on, neither of them the archive

readableDescriptions.text: This is the passage the masons used, never finished and never sealed. Someone has already been through the grave goods stacked along it, and what they left behind is worth carrying out on the way back.

requiredFeatures: sealed name registers cut into the jamb
rainwater running in from the ramp
elven public-purpose plan with no idols
one clear way back to the ramp

readableDescriptions.text: Past the bronze door the jamb carries register after register of sealed names, each one struck through and cut again below. Nothing here is a shrine: the elves built the place to keep an account, and the account is still open.

value.description: The wreck coast and its jungle approaches. Steam-warped debris, black sand and old elven roadwork make a crowded edge between the sea and the island interior.
